answer: At the saw pit the sawyer and his mate pull the great saw together, and the kerf must run straight or the plank is lost. Proof of pewterer plate via tin assay tally is the pulling: a plate the pewterer casts only after the tin assays 7 marks fine, each assay struck by the pewterer himself. The marble is the first kerf, cut at the butt end; the quill is the tally, kept on a board nailed to the pit wall; the sonnet is the pit itself, dug by the sawyer's father. A cheat must cut 21 false kerfs and saw 21 false planks, and the board still shows no tally under his name.
